An attacker who creates fake identities cannot know which fake peers will grade which submissions, so a fixed collusion ring rarely lands on the same item, and buying influence would require controlling a large fraction of the entire pool at every epoch, which scales its cost with the honest majority. Reputation-staked agents risk slashing if caught grading dishonestly, so a bribe must exceed expected loss.
